finalText:
Priya Raman's order O-3001 has been fully processed. She has been refunded the full £686.00 (68,600 cents) she paid: £137.00 went back to her card and £548.00 was added to her store credit. The order now shows as returned.

**Line by line:**
- **L3, USB-C Hub (P-HUB) × 2, £138.00: cancelled.** It never shipped, so it counts as a cancellation, not a return. I refunded £138.00 to her original card (RF-1) and put both units back in stock, which took P-HUB from 8 to 10. Nothing on the order or the product said this line was backordered, so I treated its stock as set aside.
- **L1 (P-DOC, £219.00) and L2 (P-MON, £329.00): returned.** Both shipped on 2026-05-04. The return policy allows 30 days from shipping, and both lines are well past that. Outside the window the policy says the refund must be store credit, never the card. I recorded £548.00 as a store-credit refund on the order (RF-2) and added the same amount to her balance, which went from £5.00 to £553.00.

**Checks:**
- No line was refunded more than she paid for it, and nothing had been refunded before.
- The shipping address and ship dates are unchanged.
- No other order, customer or product was touched.
- I did **not** restock the dock or the monitor. They go back into stock only when the warehouse confirms it has received them.

**Date mismatch:** the task says today is 2026-10-05, but the system reports 2026-07-25. It made no difference: either way, more than 30 days have passed since 2026-05-04, so both returned lines had to be paid as store credit.
